content.intro: In this lesson, you will work through where is jquery used? with a focused jQuery example. The subtopics below preserve the supplied curriculum coverage and connect the API idea to a small browser interface.
content.why_it_matters: This topic is useful because it turns traditional multipage websites into a repeatable implementation choice. jQuery is a JavaScript library that wraps common DOM, event, effect, and request tasks in a concise, chainable API. It complements JavaScript rather than replacing it.

common_mistakes: Assuming a selector matched an element without checking the collection length.
Confusing jQuery collections with native DOM elements or live properties with markup attributes.
Using .html() with untrusted data or assuming client-side validation enforces server rules.
